articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now supports Microsoft Azure platform logs, metrics and traces
articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now supports collecting Azure resource logs, Azure Monitor platform metrics, virtual network (VNet) flow logs, and traces from Application Insights. Teams that run workloads on both AWS and Azure no longer need separate monitoring tools or custom pipelines to see their whole environment. Central operations, DevOps, and site reliability engineering (SRE) teams can now view Azure telemetry alongside their AWS telemetry in one place. To get started, connect a Microsoft Entra ID tenant to your AWS account and Region. You can choose the telemetry types, subscriptions, Azure regions, resource types, and tags to collect. Azure telemetry lands in Amazon CloudWatch, and Omni spaces can monitor applications and infrastructure across cloud providers. For example, during an incident you can trace a slow request from an Azure-hosted service to its AWS dependencies without switching consoles. You can set up the connectors in the Amazon CloudWatch Omni console or with the AWS CLI. Azure telemetry collection is available in all Azure Public Regions and can be ingested to all regions where CloudWatch Omni is available. To get started, visit the CloudWatch Omni User Guide and for pricing visit pricing page.
articles.summary: CloudWatch Omni agrège désormais les logs, métriques et traces Azure dans AWS pour une surveillance unifiée multi-cloud.

articles.title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock expands language support and country-aware search
articles.excerpt: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock, the tool that grounds AI agents and applications in cited, current web information, now supports five new languages, plus non-US English, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock: Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Japanese. Agents serving users in these languages get results that draw on local-language sources. We are also introducing a new optional country field that biases results toward sources from a specific country - just pass an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as “JP” or “DE”. This is useful for agents that serve users in multiple countries, for questions whose answer depends on the user's actual or preferred location (e.g., local regulations, prices or public officials), and for surfacing regional sources. Both the expanded language support and the optional country field are available today in every Region where Web Search is offered: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland) for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and US Regions for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock. Queries are processed in the Region you call, helping organizations meet data residency requirements. Existing customers get the new language capabilities automatically, with no code changes, and pricing is the same in every language. To get started with Web Search on Amazon Bedrock, checkout the developer guide and the web search product page .
articles.summary: Web Search sur Amazon Bedrock supporte désormais 5 nouvelles langues et un filtrage par pays pour des résultats locaux.

articles.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Primary Endpoint
articles.excerpt: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now provides a Primary Endpoint, a DNS name that always resolves to the current primary DB instance in a replica configuration. When you switch over to an Oracle replica, Amazon RDS points the Primary Endpoint to the new primary DB instance, so you don't need to change your application connection strings. Previously, after each switchover, you had to update connection strings or DNS records to point to the new primary DB instance, which often required change approvals and coordination across teams. With Primary Endpoint, you can run planned switchovers, such as disaster recovery drills, to replicas in the same AWS Region or to cross-Region replicas without changing your application configuration. If your applications connect through the Primary Endpoint, you don't need to update their connection strings after the switchover. Every RDS for Oracle Enterprise Edition DB instance has a Primary Endpoint at no additional charge, and you don't have to create it. The Primary Endpoint is provided in addition to the instance endpoint, so your existing applications aren't affected. Primary Endpoint is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more, see Using the Primary Endpoint for Amazon RDS for Oracle in the Amazon RDS User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon RDS pour Oracle propose un Primary Endpoint qui redirige automatiquement vers l'instance principale après un basculement, sans modifier les chaînes de connexion.

articles.title: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge
articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge . Lambda emits an event each time an Event Function version changes state because of a customer action, such as creating, updating, publishing, or deleting a function. These events help platform and DevOps teams to trigger automation as soon as a function becomes ready to invoke, an update finishes, or an operation fails, without polling the GetFunction API. Customers use Lambda Event Functions to build APIs, event processing workloads, multi-step workflows, and data pipelines. As organizations grow to thousands of functions, platform teams need to know when a function changes state so they can take the next step. For example, a deployment pipeline can run integration tests and then shift alias traffic once a new version becomes active. Until now, these tools had to poll the GetFunction API to track state changes. Polling consumed API quota, slowed down pipelines, and required custom retry logic, which added operational overhead. With this launch, you can create EventBridge rules that match on fields such as the function ARN, detail type, or state, and route matched events to targets such as AWS Step Functions , AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS , or Amazon SQS . This helps you build reliable, event-driven deployment pipelines across all of your functions, without writing or maintaining custom polling logic. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions . You can create rules by using the EventBridge console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), or AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM). Lambda publishes these events automatically at no additional cost. Standard pricing applies to the targets that your EventBridge rules invoke. To learn more, see the AWS Lambda Developer Guide and the Amazon EventBridge User Guide.
articles.summary: AWS Lambda publie désormais ses changements d'état de fonctions vers EventBridge, éliminant le besoin de polling pour les pipelines automatisés.

articles.title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated Internet firewall in public preview
articles.excerpt: AWS Network Firewall announces the public preview of automated Internet firewall, a new centralized control that allows you to configure Network Firewall, with native network address translation (NAT) capability, on the internet gateways of all the Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) in your environment. Using automated Internet firewall mode, you can centrally define your Network Firewall security rules and enforce them on all inbound and outbound traffic across the internet gateways of your VPCs. You are not required to make routing or architectural changes to deploy automated Internet firewall. You can deploy it across select VPCs or your entire account, organization or organization unit. AWS Network Firewall is a stateful, managed, network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for your VPC. Customers use it to inspect their traffic and secure AWS resources. Prior to this launch, customers would configure AWS Network Firewalls inside their VPCs in the traffic path of all internet communication to achieve thorough security coverage against the threats on the internet. They deployed Network Firewall endpoints in dedicated subnets and made route updates for every subnet that needed internet access across all their VPCs. In addition, they monitored the environment to ensure that no new internet network paths bypassed these security controls. Automated Internet firewall makes this deployment and management simpler. You just define and maintain filtering rules, and AWS enforces it directly at the internet gateway of every VPC in scope, ensuring that all intended traffic entering or leaving your VPCs via the internet gateway is inspected. Automated Internet firewall comes with built-in NAT functionality for your egress-only internet connectivity needs. You can use it to filter traffic, perform NAT and log all internet activity across all internet gateways. You don't need to make architectural changes inside every VPC or monitor every internet network path. A
articles.summary: AWS Network Firewall propose un mode automatisé pour sécuriser les passerelles internet de tous les VPC sans modification d'architecture.

articles.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Replica First Patching for reduced downtime
articles.excerpt: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports Replica First Patching, which reduces downtime during minor version upgrades. Replica First Patching is available for Enterprise Edition DB instances. With Replica First Patching, you apply a minor version upgrade to a replica in the same AWS Region first while your primary DB instance continues to serve traffic, and then switch over to the replica when you're ready to complete the upgrade. If the replica is in read-only mode, you can validate the new minor engine version with your read traffic. Replica First Patching helps you keep mission-critical Oracle workloads current on minor versions with less disruption. You choose when to switch over within the switchover window, for example during a low-traffic period. If you don't switch over within the window, Amazon RDS rolls back the replica to its original minor engine version. After the switchover, Amazon RDS completes the upgrade on the new primary DB instance. Amazon RDS then upgrades your other replicas, including your former primary DB instance, to the same minor engine version. We recommend that you connect your applications through the Primary Endpoint when you use Replica First Patching. The Primary Endpoint is a DNS name that resolves to the current primary DB instance, so your applications reach the new primary DB instance after the switchover without connection string changes. Replica First Patching is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. Standard pricing applies to the replica DB instance. To learn more, see Upgrading with Replica First Patching in the Amazon RDS User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon RDS pour Oracle permet de réduire les temps d'arrêt des mises à jour mineures via Replica First Patching, disponible gratuitement pour l'Enterprise Edition.

articles.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to additional AWS Regions
articles.excerpt: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports additional AWS Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes, and MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate your user data to Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Hong Kong, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, New Zealand, Osaka, Taipei, Thailand), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan, Spain, Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Mexico (Central), Africa (Cape Town) Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your needs. MRR is available as an add-on for user pools on the Essentials or Plus feature plans, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). For the full list of AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region . To get started, visit the developer guide for instructions and the pricing page for pricing details.
articles.summary: Amazon Cognito étend sa réplication multi-régions à de nouvelles zones AWS, améliorant la résilience et la conformité des identités utilisateurs.

articles.title: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance and smarter scaling
articles.excerpt: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance at the same price per Neptune Capacity Unit, running on AWS Graviton4 processors. The new Graviton4-based platform also brings an improved scaling algorithm that adjusts Neptune Capacity Units (NCUs) more closely to your workload. This especially helps applications with many concurrent graph queries, such as real-time fraud detection, recommendation engines and generative AI applications that run graph lookups on every request. Neptune Serverless scales database capacity automatically as your application’s demand changes, so you can run graph applications with spiky or unpredictable traffic, such as fraud detection, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, without provisioning for peak capacity. You pay only for the capacity you use. All newly created Neptune Serverless instances will be using AWS Graviton4 processors. You can create new Neptune Serverless instances using AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI . You can upgrade existing clusters to the latest version in the next release. For more information on pricing and regional availability, refer to the Amazon Neptune pricing page and Neptune Serverless documentation .
articles.summary: Neptune Serverless d'Amazon offre jusqu'à 30% de performance en plus avec Graviton4 et un scaling plus précis pour les requêtes graphiques.

articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch extends the PromQL query window to 30 days
articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch now supports a 30-day query window for PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics, up from 7 days. You can query a month of data in a single request, chart month-over-month and week-over-week trends on one dashboard, and alarm on a 30-day baseline. Teams typically define service level objectives (SLOs) over a 30-day rolling window, longer than a 7-day query can measure. You can now calculate availability and remaining error budget for a full SLO period in one query, and alarm when a service is on track to exhaust its budget. A month of history also makes capacity forecasts more reliable, because a 7-day baseline skews to a single busy weekend. This feature is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics in Amazon CloudWatch are available. To get started, see Query OpenTelemetry metrics with PromQL in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide .
articles.summary: CloudWatch étend PromQL à 30 jours pour analyser les tendances mensuelles et calculer les SLOs en une seule requête.

articles.title: Account Mapping and Planning now available in AWS Partner Central
articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now map their target accounts against AWS records and find where to collaborate with AWS on joint go-to-market before an opportunity exists. Account Mapping and Planning in AWS Partner Central replaces manual, spreadsheet-based account mapping. Upload a target account list through CSV, API, or CRM integration, and accounts are matched automatically against AWS records, including accounts without an ACE opportunity and in any country. Partners can use Account Mapping and Planning to enrich matched accounts with AWS Marketplace propensity insights, solution-level purchase likelihood, and eligibility for programs such as the Partner Greenfield Program and the Partner-Led Sales Motion. This helps Partners prioritize high-propensity and program-eligible accounts for go-to-market activity. Eligible Partners can also request joint account planning with AWS sales on accounts marked Qualified, so AWS and Partner teams can align on an account strategy earlier. Account planning is available to Consulting Partners that are ACE-eligible, Premier tier and managed by an AWS Partner Development Manager (PDM), and to ISVs that are ACE-eligible, enrolled in the SaaS Co-sell Benefit program and PDM-managed. Account Mapping and Planning is available under the Sell tab in AWS Partner Central, and account matching and enrichment are open to all ACE-eligible Partners. Partners can work in the Partner Central console, through the API and SDK, through the Partner Central MCP server, or through an integration Partner to connect results to their CRM. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central, go to the Account Mapping page under the Sell tab, and upload a target account list.
articles.summary: AWS Partners automatisent le mapping de comptes cibles via AWS Partner Central pour prioriser les opportunités commerciales.

articles.title: Demand Center now available in AWS Partner Central
articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now plan, launch, fund, and measure demand generation campaigns in one AI-powered experience. Demand Center in AWS Partner Central succeeds Marketing Central and brings together Marketing Central and MDF capabilities, letting you work in Partner Central, in your CRM, or in your AI agents. Create hero and distribution assets in multiple languages in minutes with AI campaign creation. Generate content from reference materials, a URL, or a description, and launch it across email, social, and banner ads. Upload leads to get them enriched with propensity signals and recommended next actions. Choose from ready-to-run Partner Ready Campaign kits or connect with AWS-vetted agencies through Agency Connect. Generate case studies with AI from ACE closed-won opportunities, and tailor campaign content to the leads included in each campaign. Connect your CRM or marketing automation tool agent-to-agent, or use Demand Center inside agents such as AWS Quick through the Partner Central MCP server. Track campaign-to-revenue performance in Partner Analytics. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and select Demand Center.
articles.summary: AWS Partners gèrent campagnes marketing IA dans Partner Central avec création IA, enrichissement leads et suivi revenus.

articles.title: Lead groups and channel recommendations now available in AWS Partner Central
articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now organize enriched leads and plan outreach with lead groups and channel recommendations in AWS Partner Central. Enriched leads are automatically grouped by solution area and segmented into sales-ready, marketing-ready, and limited-potential groups, so you no longer have to segment leads by hand. Limited-potential leads help you avoid spending time and budget on leads unlikely to convert, lowering your cost of acquiring new customers. For each enriched lead, you also get guidance on whether phone or email may be more effective, along with AI-generated call scripts and email scripts to act on it. Marketing-ready lead groups can be sent to Demand Center to create assets and launch targeted campaigns. Sales-ready leads can be exported to the Partner's CRM for direct outreach. Lead groups and channel recommendations are available to ACE-eligible Partners on the Leads page in AWS Partner Central and through the AWS Partner Central Selling API. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and go to the Leads page.
articles.summary: AWS Partner Central propose désormais des groupes de leads enrichis et des recommandations de canaux pour optimiser l'acquisition clients.

articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch EKS Container Insights now offers built-in monitoring for open source Kubernetes tools
articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces built-in monitoring for open source tools running on your Amazon EKS clusters, including Karpenter, KEDA, vLLM, KServe, SGLang, Ray and Knative Serving. You get dashboards for the tools you already use without running Prometheus or Grafana yourself. Monitoring starts automatically when you enable OTel Container Insights. For your AI inference workloads, you can see queued requests, time to first token, and KV cache usage for each model server. For autoscaling, you can see which scalers are failing and how long your scale loop takes. CloudWatch tags every metric with its pod, workload, and node, so you can trace a slow model server to the node it runs on. These EKS solutions are available in version 8.0.0 and later of the add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Metrics are charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Solutions in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.
articles.summary: CloudWatch EKS Container Insights surveille désormais nativement les outils open source Kubernetes (Karpenter, KEDA, etc.) sans Prometheus/Grafana.

articles.title: AWS Quick now supports group assignments for custom permissions and limit profiles
articles.excerpt: AWS Quick now supports assignments for custom permissions and limit profiles to groups from your enterprise identity provider (IdP). Administrators can now apply feature restrictions and per-user resource limits to IdP groups, in addition to the existing user, role, and account assignments. Organizations can align governance with their enterprise identity structure without maintaining assignments for individual users. Administrators manage user, account or group assignments in the Quick administration console or through new policy assignment APIs. For example, an organization can assign its finance group a custom permissions profile that blocks members from creating agents, or apply Deny by Default so that, within selected feature categories, the group can use only capabilities an administrator explicitly allows. Administrators can also assign a limit profile to a group to set each member’s index capacity and agent hours. Quick enforces these limits automatically as users consume resources. When group-level assignments apply to a user who belongs to multiple groups, Quick resolves overlapping assignments as follows: for custom permissions, a capability denied by any group stays denied, and for limit profiles, the user receives the highest value for each limit type across those groups. Group assignments are available in Quick for Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature availability by AWS Region, see AWS Quick Regions . To learn more, see the custom permissions and limit profiles documentation.
articles.summary: AWS Quick permet désormais d'attribuer des permissions et limites personnalisées par groupes IdP, simplifiant la gouvernance sans gestion individuelle.

articles.title: AWS Quick introduces enterprise guardrails (preview)
articles.excerpt: AWS Quick now includes enterprise guardrails, giving administrators configurable content safety and sensitive-information controls for user prompts. Administrators can apply guardrail policies to individual users or enterprise identity provider (IdP) groups or set a policy as the account default. User-level policies take precedence over group policies and account defaults. When multiple group policies apply, Quick combines their content restrictions, using the stricter setting when controls overlap. Administrators create guardrail policies in the Quick administration console using content filters, denied topics, blocked words and phrases, prompt-attack detection, and controls for selected types of personally identifiable information (PII). For example, an administrator can create a policy that blocks prompts containing confidential project names and assign it to an IdP group. Detect-only mode lets administrators test prompt-filtering rules against real production traffic before enforcing them. In this mode, Quick evaluates user prompts and logs policy matches without blocking requests, so administrators can assess the impact on business workflows and refine policies. When administrators enable enforcement, Quick blocks matching prompts and displays a message to the user. Administrators can review detected and blocked events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Enterprise guardrails are available in preview for select Quick customers with Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature availability by AWS Region, see AWS Quick Regions . To learn more, see the enterprise guardrails documentation .
articles.summary: AWS Quick ajoute des garde-fous configurables pour contrôler la sécurité des prompts et les données sensibles des utilisateurs en entreprise.

articles.title: AWS announces Data Hub in AWS Billing and Cost Management (preview)
articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces the preview of Data Hub in AWS Billing and Cost Management, a managed data layer that enables AWS FinOps Agent to query cost and usage data with SQL. In preview, Data Hub is available to AWS FinOps Agent, so the agent can identify the individual resources behind a cost change, break down spend by team or cost allocation tag, and show how a resource's cost and usage change hour by hour. With AWS FinOps Agent and Data Hub, customers get these answers without setting up a data export or building and maintaining a cost data pipeline. Data Hub provides 13 months of hourly, resource-level cost and usage data in the published CUR 2.0 schema, including resource identifiers and cost allocation tags. AWS provisions the data, refreshes data daily, and maintains the schema as new services, commitments, and charge types are added. When set up from the management account, Data Hub covers cost and usage data across the accounts in your organization. Data Hub (preview) is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region and covers cost and usage data across regions. There is no charge for Data Hub during preview. To learn more about Data Hub, see the AWS Billing and Cost Management User Guide and the launch blog . You can get started from the Data Hub page in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console or from the AWS FinOps Agent console.
articles.summary: AWS lance Data Hub pour interroger en SQL les coûts et usages par ressource sans pipeline dédié.

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825)
articles.excerpt: On November 19, 2026, the Ruby team disclosed ruby2shell ( CVE-2026-132825 ), a heap buffer overflow in the way Ruby changes the case of strings. Ruby rates the flaw Critical and says it is aware of proofs of concept that achieve remote code execution in some scenarios. Fixes shipped in Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10 . The reach is wide. Veria Labs reports that Ruby on Rails and classic-style Sinatra applications reach the bug in their default configuration, before any authentication. Self-hosted products that bundle Ruby, including GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject, Discourse and Chatwoot, shipped an affected Ruby in their latest release at the time of disclosure. Cloudflare WAF blocks ruby2shell for all customers, including those on the Free plan. We have added two rules to both the Cloudflare Free Managed Ruleset and the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, with Block as the default action: one for ruby2shell and one for GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px, a related integer overflow in Ruby string case conversion fixed in the same releases. The WAF is a compensating control, not a replacement for patching. Exploits can reach the bug through paths a WAF does not see, and the only complete fix is to upgrade Ruby. Our team continues to monitor attack traffic and will update the rules as new techniques appear. You can track rule changes in the WAF changelog and get the latest on the vulnerability in the Cloudflare Zero Wire briefing . Cloudflare has patched its own systems that use Ruby, and we have found no indication of compromise. What we know about ruby2shell Ruby strings carry an encoding, and Ruby still supports many legacy single-byte encodings, such as ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) and Windows-1252, alongside UTF-8. In a single-byte encoding each character takes one byte, so changing the case of a string usually produces output of the same length. The German sharp s (ß) breaks that assumption. articles.summary: Cloudflare WAF bloque l'exploitation de ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825) via deux règles pour tous ses clients.

articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports custom OpenTelemetry and Prometheus telemetry
articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for your own application telemetry in the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on. The CloudWatch agent you already run now accepts metrics, traces, and logs from your applications, so you don't deploy and operate a separate collector to get them into CloudWatch. Applications instrumented with an OpenTelemetry SDK send to an OTLP endpoint that the agent serves on every node, on by default. Metrics arrive as CloudWatch metrics you query with PromQL, traces go to AWS X-Ray and Transaction Search, and logs go to CloudWatch Logs. For Prometheus metrics, the agent scrapes the targets described by standard ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor objects, with no Prometheus operator to run and no change to your scrape configuration. Each team defines its own targets alongside its application rather than in one central add-on configuration. Label selectors let you choose which monitors CloudWatch scrapes. Both sources carry the same Kubernetes, host, cloud, and service attributes the add-on applies to the pod they came from, so you can join application telemetry to your cluster metrics. Custom telemetry is available in version 8.0.0 and later of the EKS add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Telemetry is charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Custom telemetry in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.
articles.summary: CloudWatch EKS add-on accepte désormais des métriques, traces et logs personnalisés via OpenTelemetry et Prometheus sans collecteur externe.

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against phpAfterShell and other critical PHP flaws
articles.excerpt: On November 19, 2026, the security research company depthfirst disclosed phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714) , a vulnerability in PHP's default file-based session handler that can lead to remote code execution. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The PHP project fixed it the same day in versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, and 8.6.0. These releases fix 16 other security vulnerabilities, six of them also rated critical. Cloudflare’s web application firewall (WAF) blocks known phpAfterShell attack patterns, including for customers on the Free plan. The protection comes from a PHP remote code execution rule we first deployed in October 2026 for the php2shell vulnerabilities. That rule already detected part of the phpAfterShell attack pattern before the vulnerability was disclosed, and on November 19 we updated its detection logic to cover phpAfterShell. The rule is part of both the Cloudflare Free Managed Ruleset and the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, is enabled by default, and its default action is Block. In the same WAF release, we added three new rules to the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset for paid plans: one for a request smuggling flaw in PHP-FPM (CVE-2026-129289), and two for flaws in PHP's SOAP extension (CVE-2026-15353 and CVE-2026-129506) that PHP fixed in the same releases. These rules are enabled by default with the Log action, because the request patterns they look for can also appear in legitimate traffic, and blocking by default could disrupt it. Customers can review matching requests in Security Events now and change the action to Block once they confirm the rules do not affect legitimate traffic. The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch. Several of the critical flaws depend on server configuration or can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, and the only complete fix is to upgrade PHP and restart every worker. Our analysts continue to monitor attack act
articles.summary: Cloudflare WAF bloque phpAfterShell et 4 autres failles PHP critiques via des règles par défaut, protégeant même les utilisateurs gratuits.

articles.title: Amazon DynamoDB vector search now supports new inline filter operators
articles.excerpt: Amazon DynamoDB vector search inline filters now support range comparisons, value lists, and logical operators in addition to the equality operator, so you can narrow a vector search to exactly the items you want. You can now filter on numeric ranges such as price, rating, or publish date, match an attribute against a list of values, check whether an attribute exists, and combine conditions with OR and NOT. Amazon DynamoDB vector indexes store vector embeddings alongside your operational data, and the SearchVectors API returns the items whose embeddings are most similar to your query vector. The search condition expression in a SearchVectors request now accepts the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, and BETWEEN on Number attributes, the IN operator, the attribute_exists and attribute_not_exists functions, and the logical operators AND, OR, and NOT. DynamoDB applies the filter during the search, so every result it returns matches. For example, a retail application can return the products most similar to a shopper's query within a price range and a set of brands, and a retrieval-augmented generation application can limit results to selected document categories published after a given date. The new operators are available in all AWS Regions where DynamoDB vector search is available. To learn more, see vector search in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, or visit the Amazon DynamoDB page.
articles.summary: DynamoDB vector search ajoute des filtres avancés (comparaisons, listes, opérateurs logiques) pour affiner les résultats vectoriels directement.

articles.title: Amazon Transcribe announces a synchronous transcription API
articles.excerpt: Amazon Transcribe now offers a synchronous transcription API, TranscribeAudio . Send a complete audio file in a single request and get the full transcript back in the same response. There is no job to start, no status to poll, no connection to manage. The transcripts are as accurate as Amazon Transcribe batch transcription, so you can add fast, accurate speech-to-text to interactive applications such as voice assistants, agent-assist tools and on-demand "transcribe this clip" features. The synchronous API supports the Amazon Transcribe features you already use, including: Word-level timestamps and smart formatting for numbers, dates, currency and phone numbers Automatic language identification Speaker diarization, and channel identification for up to two channels Custom vocabulary and vocabulary filtering, which you can provide directly in the request with no setup step PII redaction Send audio inline (up to 25 MB) or from Amazon S3 (up to 500 MB), 0.5 seconds to 1 hour long, in WAV, MP3, FLAC, M4A, MP4, Ogg, WebM or AMR format. The transcript comes back in the response, or Transcribe can write it to an S3 location you choose. Pricing is $0.0070 per minute of audio, billed per second, with speaker diarization, language identification, custom vocabulary and channel identification included. Two-channel audio is billed once on file duration. PII redaction is available as an add-on. Supports English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified, Traditional and Hong Kong). Available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland, London, Frankfurt), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Seoul) and South America (São Paulo), with PII redaction available in all stated Regions except South America (São Paulo). To get started, see Amazon Transcribe API Reference and the Amazon Transcribe pricing page .
articles.summary: Amazon Transcribe propose une API de transcription synchrone instantanée pour applications interactives, sans gestion de jobs ni polling.

articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports telemetry filtering
articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces telemetry filtering for the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, so you can stop paying to ingest telemetry you don't use. You can now set cluster-wide include and exclude lists for namespaces, metric names, and pod and node labels. Exclude the non-production namespaces you don't monitor, drop high-cardinality metrics by name, and keep only the labels you group by rather than every label on every resource. Because ingestion is billed per GB, collecting less lowers what you pay, and you can adjust filters with a single add-on configuration update as your clusters change. Telemetry filtering is available in version 8.0.0 and later of the EKS add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Telemetry sent through the add-on is charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide .
articles.summary: CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on permet désormais de filtrer les télémétries pour réduire les coûts d'ingestion en sélectionnant les données utiles.

articles.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard to compare models on quality, speed, and cost
articles.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard in Amazon SageMaker Studio. You can use it to compare foundation models side by side on throughput, latency, and cost, and then deploy or customize the model that fits your workload. Comparing models has usually meant reading model cards one at a time and relying on benchmark scores that different sources published under different conditions. The JumpStart leaderboard puts consistent measurements in one view. AWS evaluates every model on three reasoning benchmarks, BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU-Pro, using the same evaluation setup for each model. AWS also measures time to first token, throughput, and instance cost on SageMaker for each JumpStart deployment configuration. You can use all of the filters already available for JumpStart models, such as model provider, license, and input and output modality, to narrow the list. You can also choose a use case profile and an optimization goal (balanced, cost, latency, or throughput) to see the metrics for the configuration you plan to deploy. At launch, the leaderboard covers more than 70 LLMs from providers including Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM, and Arcee. The JumpStart model leaderboard is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is available. To get started, open SageMaker JumpStart in SageMaker Studio and choose the Leaderboard view. To learn more, see JumpStart leaderboard methodology and read the launch blog post .
articles.summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart propose un tableau de bord comparant 70+ modèles d'IA sur performance, coût et latence pour faciliter leur sélection et déploiement.

articles.title: AWS Partner Central Agents now help partners create and manage Partner Central and Marketplace support cases
articles.excerpt: AWS Partner Central Agents now help AWS Partners create and manage AWS Partner Central and AWS Marketplace support cases in one place. The agents are available 24/7 and draw on Partner Central account details and authoritative, partner-specific knowledge from AWS to resolve most inquiries instantly. If a inquiry needs a support engineer, the agents will gather details and create a case. This reduces the time partners spend looking for help, and gives support teams the context they need to resolve cases faster. Partners can handle a case from start to finish in one chat, with the full record in AWS Support Center. To create a case, partners can start describing their issue to AWS Partner Central Agents or use the prompt "get support." The agents gather additional details necessary to resolve the case, set the category, and draft the description. Partners review and submit the case, and the agents route the case to the right support team. In the same chat, partners can view case communications, track progress, post replies, and add attachments. With this launch, Partner Central and AWS Marketplace cases also move to AWS Support Center. There, partners can view the full case history and translate support correspondence into Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. The new support experience is available today to all AWS Partners and AWS Marketplace sellers in the AWS Partner Central console and through the AWS Partner Central Agents MCP server. With the MCP server, partners can bring the support experience into tools such as Kiro, AWS Quick, CRM systems, and other AI clients. To learn more, see Getting support in AWS Partner Central , Getting support for AWS Marketplace , and Getting started with the Partner Central Agents MCP server .
articles.summary: AWS Partner Central Agents automatisent la création et gestion des cas de support Partner Central et Marketplace, réduisant les délais de résolution.

articles.title: Spend limits in the new AWS experience now support SMS alerts
articles.excerpt: Builders using the new AWS experience on the Paid plan can now receive spend limit alerts by text message (SMS), alongside existing email notifications. A spend limit sets the maximum monthly cost for a project. Notifications are sent as a project approaches its limit, and when a project reaches its limit, AWS automatically pauses it. SMS gives builders a second way to stay informed about their project costs. Email alerts can go unnoticed when builders are away from their inbox, leaving little time to respond before a project is paused. SMS alerts close this gap with a text message when a project's actual costs reach 90% of its spend limit, so builders have time to act, such as raising the limit or stopping resources they don't need. To turn on SMS alerts, verify your mobile phone number in AWS Settings and turn on text alerts for spend limits. Text alerts are only sent to verified numbers, and you can opt out at any time. SMS alerts for spend limits are available at no additional charge for US phone numbers, including Puerto Rico, Guam, the US Virgin Islands, and American Samoa. To learn more, see Create a spend limit in AWS Settings , the AWS Account Management Reference Guide , or Get started with AWS .
articles.summary: AWS permet désormais des alertes SMS pour les limites de dépenses, en plus des emails, afin d'éviter les dépassements automatiques.

articles.title: Amazon S3 Vectors raises the filterable metadata limit to 40 KB per vector
articles.excerpt: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports up to 40 KB of filterable metadata per vector, up from 2 KB. You can attach and filter on more attributes per vector, such as category, permissions, timestamps, and descriptive tags, so your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications can narrow results by more of the fields that matter to them. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. With this launch, indexes in new vector buckets support the higher limit by default, with no change to how you write vectors with PutVectors or run filtered queries with QueryVectors. To use the higher limit on an existing index, update it in place to enhanced index mode with the UpdateIndexMode API. The higher filterable metadata limit is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or the Amazon S3 console. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 Vectors documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon S3 Vectors porte la limite de métadonnées filtrables à 40 Ko par vecteur, améliorant la précision des requêtes RAG et recherche sémantique.

articles.title: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions
articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions in AWS Trusted Advisor . These recommendations identify on-demand functions where moving to Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) is estimated to reduce costs, and provide configuration guidance for running on LMI. With these recommendations, you can lower your Lambda costs by focusing your efforts on the functions with the greatest estimated savings. LMI lets you run Lambda functions on Amazon EC2 instances while maintaining the operational simplicity of Lambda. With LMI, you can access specialized compute configurations and drive cost efficiency through EC2 pricing options such as Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, without managing infrastructure. Previously, to determine whether a function was a good fit for LMI, you had to analyze its invocation patterns, estimate LMI costs, and select the right instance type and memory-to-vCPU ratio yourself. This manual process added overhead and delayed savings. With this launch, Lambda automatically analyzes the invocation patterns, duration, and resource utilization of your high-volume Event Functions and recommends those where LMI is estimated to reduce costs. Estimates are based on a simulation of each function's invocation patterns, using public Lambda pricing and Amazon EC2 On-Demand pricing. Each recommendation includes the function ARN, the recommended EC2 instance type and memory-to-vCPU ratio, the estimated current cost, the estimated LMI cost, and the estimated savings. You can use the recommended configuration to run a function on LMI without sizing it yourself and realize cost savings sooner. These recommendations are available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), and Europe (Milan). Customers with eligible AWS Support plans can access them in the Trusted Advisor console alongside other cost optimization checks. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Developer Guide, the AWS Trusted Advisor U
articles.summary: AWS Lambda propose désormais des recommandations d'optimisation des coûts pour les fonctions événementielles via Trusted Advisor.

articles.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases
articles.excerpt: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases, powered by AWS Glue Data Quality, which profiles and evaluates your tables at catalog scale from a single configuration. You define data quality checks once for a catalog, a database, or a single table, and AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you choose. Quality issues surface as data changes, without per-table setup or manual runs, which helps keep bad data from reaching downstream consumers. You can use built-in profiling options that AWS Glue provides for common baseline statistics or provide your own Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL) ruleset with analyzers, rules, or both to hold every table in a database to the same quality standards. You have the flexibility to run evaluations once when you create the configuration or set up triggers, so evaluations run on a schedule or whenever table metadata changes, including every Apache Iceberg commit. After three runs on a table, AWS Glue Data Quality flags anomalous statistics that drift outside expected bounds, surfacing changes that no rule covers. Results are accessible through the existing AWS Glue Data Quality APIs, or you can opt-in to write them to Apache Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog or to Amazon S3. Data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases in AWS Glue Data Catalog is available in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS China regions. To get started, create a data quality configuration by using the AWS CLI, API, or SDKs, which support built-in profiling and custom DQDL rulesets at the catalog, database, or table level. In Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, you can turn on profiling for a catalog or database from the catalog page. To learn more, visit the AWS Glue Data Quality documentation and the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio documentation .
articles.summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog surveille automatiquement la qualité des données dans les catalogues et bases de données via des règles configurables et des alertes sur anomalies.

articles.title: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon SQS FIFO queues
articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue event source mappings (ESMs) in provisioned mode , up from 10 messages previously. With larger batches, you can process high-volume, ordered workloads such as financial transactions, order processing, and inventory updates with fewer invocations and higher throughput. Lambda continues to preserve message ordering within each message group. Customers use SQS FIFO queues with Lambda to build event-driven applications that need strict message ordering and deduplication. With provisioned mode for SQS ESMs, you can use throughput controls to set a minimum and maximum number of event pollers to meet strict performance requirements. Previously, provisioned mode customers who needed higher throughput for SQS FIFO queues were limited by the maximum batch size of 10 messages. This required them to scale out invocations or add custom buffering logic, which added operational overhead and cost. With this launch, you can set a batch size of up to 10,000 messages and a batching window of up to 300 seconds for FIFO queues, so you can process large volumes of ordered messages in fewer invocations without re-architecting your applications. This feature is available for SQS FIFO ESMs in provisioned mode in all AWS commercial Regions. You can configure the batch size and the batching window when you create new ESMs or update existing ESMs by using the Lambda console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK, or AWS SAM. You can also use coding assistants such as Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex with the Agent Toolkit for AWS. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Developer Guide and the AWS Lambda pricing .
articles.summary: AWS Lambda supporte désormais des lots de 10 000 messages pour SQS FIFO, améliorant le débit et réduisant les coûts d'invocations.

articles.title: AWS Pricing Calculator now estimates workload costs through a new API
articles.excerpt: AWS Pricing Calculator now offers GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost, a new API that returns the estimated cost of a planned workload in a single API call. You send up to 500 usage lines in one request and get the cost back right away, without saving an estimate to your account. While workload estimates let you create and save an estimate in Pricing Calculator, GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost returns a cost on demand, directly in your own tools and workflows. You can choose from three rate types: public On-Demand rates, your rates after discounts, or your rates after discounts plus Savings Plans and Reserved Instances. The API returns the cost of each line and the total. For example, you can check what a design will cost before you deploy it, or let an AI coding agent call the API to price a workload while it helps you design it. GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost is generally available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions, except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost in the AWS Billing and Cost Management API Reference, or visit the AWS Pricing Calculator product page .
articles.summary: AWS propose une API pour estimer en temps réel les coûts d'un workload avant déploiement, intégrée directement dans les outils.

articles.title: AWS Billing and Cost Management now offers APIs to track payment status
articles.excerpt: Today, AWS Billing and Cost Management announces new APIs that let you view your AWS payment information through the AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI. With these APIs, you can check your account balance, find invoices that are due or past due, see which payments and credit memos were applied to each invoice, and confirm that the payment methods on your account are active. You can call the APIs from your own tools or through an AI agent. Previously, finance teams had to sign in to the console to find past-due invoices, match payments to invoices, or check whether a payment method was still active. Now you can automate these checks with APIs such as GetFinancialRecord, BatchGetFinancialRecord, ListFinancialRecords, GetAccountBalance, GetPaymentInstrument and ListPaymentInstruments. You can integrate the APIs with your accounts payable systems to monitor past-due balances and reconcile AWS invoices on your own schedule. The APIs are available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and available to customers in all commercial AWS Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS Payments API Reference .
articles.summary: AWS propose désormais des APIs pour suivre automatiquement les paiements, factures et soldes via SDK ou CLI, remplaçant les vérifications manuelles en console.

articles.title: We promoted developers into architects without informing them
articles.summary: Promouvoir des développeurs en architectes sans les prévenir crée des tensions et des malentendus dans les équipes techniques.

articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler adds 589 new API actions and event bus targets
articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler expands its AWS SDK integrations with 589 new API actions across 81 AWS services, and adds templated targets for the enhanced EventBridge Custom event bus. You can now schedule direct invocations of a broader set of AWS services without writing custom integration code. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. With a new templated target, you can schedule event delivery directly to the Custom event bus using its PutEvents or PutRawEvents API. The templated target also makes it easier to add metadata fields to each event. For example, you can send an event to your bus every night at midnight to start a reconciliation workflow, with no function in between to call the API. The new API actions are available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon EventBridge Scheduler is available, subject to the availability of each target service in the Region. The templated targets for the Custom event bus are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. To learn more, see Using templated targets in EventBridge Scheduler and Using universal targets in EventBridge Scheduler in the Amazon EventBridge Scheduler User Guide. Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler ajoute 589 actions API et cibles de bus personnalisé, simplifiant l'automatisation sans code.

articles.title: AWS CloudFormation Service-Managed StackSets adds custom execution roles with nested stacks support
articles.excerpt: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now supports custom execution roles for service-managed stack sets, which enables you to scope the permissions StackSets uses in each target AWS account. StackSets deploys the same infrastructure, such as networking and security settings, across thousands of accounts and Regions in one operation. With a custom execution role, you can also use nested stacks, macros, and transforms in service-managed stack sets, which allows you to deploy the reusable templates you use for individual stacks across your organization. With a custom execution role, you define what StackSets can do in each account. By default, service-managed stack sets use a role in each account that can provision any resource in a template without additional setup, and that default remains available. Now, you can provide a template that defines an IAM role, called the execution role, and StackSets creates it in each account before deploying. For example, a stack set that creates Amazon S3 buckets can use an execution role limited to CloudFormation and Amazon S3 permissions. When you update the execution role template, StackSets updates the role in every account it deployed to. To get started, choose Set execution role when you create a stack set in the CloudFormation console, or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the documentation and the AWS DevOps Blog . This feature is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. Refer to the AWS Region table for details.
articles.summary: AWS CloudFormation StackSets permet désormais des rôles d'exécution personnalisés pour des déploiements multi-comptes et multi-régions avec stacks imbriqués.

articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Webhook Events
articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge now supports Webhook Events for the enhanced Custom event bus, so SaaS applications, AI agents, and custom integrations can send events to a bus over HTTPS. You no longer need to deploy and operate your own API endpoint and compute to receive webhooks and publish them to your bus. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. When you create a webhook event source on your bus, EventBridge provides a managed HTTPS URL and verifies each request using an HMAC signature, a static token, or basic authentication. EventBridge then publishes accepted events to the bus, where Subscribers filter and deliver them like any other event. For example, shipment status updates from a logistics partner can reach your order tracking and customer notification Subscribers as soon as the partner sends them. Webhook Events are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Events received through a webhook are billed as standard Custom event bus ingress, with no additional charge for the webhook. To learn more, see Webhook Events in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: Amazon EventBridge permet désormais de recevoir des webhooks directement sur un bus personnalisé sans gérer d'infrastructure, simplifiant l'intégration d'applications tierces.

articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Amazon MSK as a target
articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) as a target for the enhanced Custom event bus, so you can deliver events to Kafka topics without running your own producer. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. To deliver events to MSK, you create a Subscriber that specifies the cluster ARN and topic. You can also configure Kafka producer settings such as partition key, acknowledgment level, and record headers. EventBridge supports both public and private, serverless and provisioned clusters. When you create a Subscriber for a private cluster, EventBridge automatically sets up a private connection to the cluster. For example, teams that publish to a shared Custom event bus can now deliver purchase-order events to the MSK topics their payments team already consumes from. Amazon MSK targets are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Delivery to MSK is billed as standard Custom event bus egress. EventBridge also supports compression before delivery, which is billed as an Event Evaluation. To learn more, see Amazon MSK cluster target in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: EventBridge permet désormais d'envoyer des événements vers Amazon MSK sans producteur Kafka dédié, simplifiant l'intégration des flux événementiels.

articles.title: Unforced Navier-Stokes Singularity and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
articles.summary: Terence Tao propose un lien entre singularités des équations de Navier-Stokes et l'hypothèse de Riemann généralisée.

articles.title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.12 is now generally available
articles.excerpt: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.12. This release includes several security enhancements and bug fixes. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by community MySQL. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.12 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon Aurora User Guide . This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL is available. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at Aurora's getting started page .
articles.summary: Aurora MySQL 8.4.12 est disponible avec correctifs de sécurité et améliorations, simplifiant les mises à jour automatiques.

articles.title: Amazon Connect Customer expands how teams track and act on service level agreements for cases
articles.excerpt: Amazon Connect Customer enhances service level agreements (SLAs) for cases, so teams can set service goals for more of their work and respond faster when a case falls behind. Admins can set SLAs on case fields beyond status, such as requiring a case’s severity to drop from high to medium within 24 hours. Admins can add an email action to SLA breach rules, so the assigned agent learns right away when a case misses its SLA. Developers can use APIs to adjust a case’s SLA deadline when the team is waiting on information from an outside party, such as a partner. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon Connect Cases étend les SLA aux champs de cas et automatise les alertes par email pour les dépassements.

articles.title: Amazon MSK Standard Brokers adds support for Apache Kafka version 4.2
articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) now supports Apache Kafka version 4.2 on Standard brokers. A key highlight of this release is Queues for Kafka, which is now production ready. With Queues, multiple consumers can process messages from the same topic partitions, which improves parallelism and throughput for workloads that need point-to-point message delivery. This release also includes Eligible Leader Replicas (ELR) enhancements that improve leader election correctness and strengthen availability. The new consumer rebalance protocol makes consumer group rebalances smoother and faster. The new Streams Rebalance Protocol extends broker-side coordination to Kafka Streams applications so tasks get assigned more efficiently. For the full list of improvements and bug fixes, see the Apache Kafka 4.2 release notes . To start using Apache Kafka 4.2 on Amazon MSK, select version 4.2.x when creating a new cluster with the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. You can also upgrade existing MSK provisioned clusters with an in-place rolling update. Amazon MSK orchestrates broker restarts to maintain availability and protect your data during the upgrade. Kafka version 4.2 support is available today in all AWS regions where Amazon MSK Standard brokers is offered. To learn how to get started, see the Amazon MSK Developer Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon MSK supporte désormais Kafka 4.2 avec files d'attente, améliorations de leader et rebalancements plus rapides.

articles.title: Amazon ECS Action Logs now cover tasks, container instances, and capacity providers
articles.excerpt: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now extends Action Logs to include tasks, container instances, clusters, and capacity providers, so you can see why your tasks failed or why your clusters didn't scale as desired. Action Logs provide detailed, timestamped records of the actions Amazon ECS performs on your behalf, and until now covered service deployments and managed daemon updates. With the expanded coverage, you can diagnose task failures and scaling issues yourself, and resolve them faster than before, without contacting AWS support. If you use Action Logs already, you receive the new events automatically with no configuration changes. When a task fails to start, Action Logs show the reason. Examples include image pull failures, missing permissions for Amazon EBS volumes, or lack of available IP addresses in the subnet. When a running task stops, you can see the container exit code and the health check that triggered the stop. For cluster infrastructure, Action Logs record container instance registration and draining, Amazon EC2 instances that fail to register with a cluster, capacity provider changes, and managed scaling actions, including when an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group reaches its maximum size. Each log entry includes the event name, log level (INFO, WARN, or ERROR), relevant resource ARNs, and a status reason. Action Logs is available in AWS Regions, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions . You can opt in at the cluster level through the Amazon ECS console or the Amazon CloudWatch vended logs APIs, and deliver logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Data Firehose. Standard pricing for each destination applies. To learn more, see Monitor Amazon ECS operations with Action Logs in the Amazon ECS Developer Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon ECS Action Logs couvre désormais tâches, instances et fournisseurs de capacité pour diagnostiquer échecs et problèmes de scaling sans support AWS.

articles.title: AWS Transform announces UI component modernization for Windows web applications
articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announced the general availability of third-party UI component porting for ASP.NET web site modernization in AWS Transform. When AWS Transform modernizes a legacy ASP.NET web site, it now detects dependencies on popular third-party UI component libraries. You can replace them with license-free Microsoft-native and open-source components, or you can keep using vendor UI libraries. AWS Transform rewrites legacy ASP.NET web sites for ASP.NET Core UI frameworks. When the AWS Transform for .NET modernization agent finds a dependency on a popular third-party UI library, it offers two options. The first option is for customers who require open-source software only. The agent replaces each proprietary control with a Microsoft-native or open-source control on the target UI framework and removes the original dependency. The second option is for customers who want to keep using vendor libraries. The agent adds code comments and next-step instructions for moving to an equivalent vendor library on the target UI framework. You then arrange licensing with the vendor and finish the port using an AI coding companion. This capability is available at no additional cost in all eight AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered: US East (N. Virginia), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Porting UI layer code in the AWS Transform User Guide.
articles.summary: AWS Transform modernise les UI ASP.NET en remplaçant ou conservant les composants tiers, via des options open-source ou propriétaires.

articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
