articles.title: AWS Transform announces support for .NET 11 and expanded project types
articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announced the general availability of .NET 11 support in AWS Transform for .NET. Support for VB.NET, desktop projects, and mobile projects, previously in preview, is also now generally available. You can modernize a broad range of Windows .NET workloads to the latest version of .NET and lower costs by running them on Linux. Modernized workloads gain the performance improvements, new C# language features, and improved diagnostics in .NET 11. AWS Transform modernizes both legacy .NET Framework applications (version 3.5 and later) and modern .NET applications (versions 5 through 10) to .NET 11. It transforms code written in C# and VB.NET. Supported project types include class libraries, console applications, ASP.NET web projects (MVC, Web API, and Web Forms), web services (ASMX and WCF), desktop applications (WinForms and WPF), mobile applications (Xamarin), unit test projects (MSTest, NUnit, and xUnit), and Windows services. You can run all transformed applications except desktop and mobile projects on Linux, which can reduce operating costs by up to 40%. This capability is available at no additional cost in all eight AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered: US East (N. Virginia), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Modernizing .NET with AWS Transform in the AWS Transform User Guide.
articles.summary: AWS Transform supporte désormais .NET 11 et modernise des workloads Windows vers Linux, réduisant les coûts jusqu'à 40%.

articles.title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports 2B active metrics and 300K rules per workspace
articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now supports up to 2 billion active metric time series and up to 300,000 total recording and alerting rules per workspace. Customers can also create multiple workspaces per account. This lets them store and analyze billions of Prometheus metrics across their organization. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service. It helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. It scales ingestion and storage automatically for high-cardinality workloads across containerized, serverless and hybrid environments. To get started, create an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace. To raise your active series or rules limits, file a service limit increase request in AWS Support Center or AWS Service Quotas. To learn more, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus user guide and the product page.
articles.summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus gère désormais 2 milliards de métriques et 300 000 règles par espace, simplifiant le monitoring à grande échelle.

articles.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS regions
articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Central), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), South America (São Paulo), and US West (N. California). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 21 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. The service enables secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 7 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. Give each user or job their own MicroVM with a dedicated HTTPS URL that supports popular connectivity protocols such as HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSockets. You can use MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit, or with your preferred Agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS . To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda MicroVMs developer guide . For information on pricing, see Lambda MicroVMs pricing . Visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page for the latest region availability.
articles.summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs est désormais disponible dans 7 nouvelles régions, portant le total à 21, pour un calcul serverless plus isolé et réactif.

articles.title: Introducing Amazon EC2 T9g instances based on Graviton5
articles.excerpt: AWS is announcing the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T9g instances, which offer the best price performance among general-purpose EC2 instances. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T9g instances deliver up to 45% better price performance compared to previous generation T4g instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, microservices, low-traffic websites, freemium services, staging and development, and short-duration compute tasks such as batch processing, event-driven functions, and CI/CD pipelines. T9g instances deliver up to 2.3x the compute performance, 1.5x higher network bandwidth, and 2.8x higher EBS bandwidth compared to T4g instances. They are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and feature the Nitro Isolation Engine, harnessing formal verification to provide mathematical assurance that customer workloads are isolated from each other and AWS operators, pioneering a new standard for mathematically proven cloud security. T9g instances use the same CPU credit system as T4g with Standard and Unlimited modes, so existing T customers can upgrade to T9g and immediately benefit from better price performance, enabling them to lower their TCO. For customers new to AWS or migrating from on-premises, T9g instances provide one of the most cost-effective entry points to run a variety of lightweight workloads. T9g.micro and T9g.small are available under the AWS Free Tier . T9g instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (N. California, Oregon), Canada (Central), South America (São Paulo), Europe (Frankfurt, Spain), and Asia Pacific (Malaysia, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo) regions. T9g instances are available to purchase via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. To
articles.summary: AWS lance les instances EC2 T9g Graviton5, 45% plus performantes et moins chères que les T4g, optimisées pour charges légères.

articles.title: Amazon MSK now supports in-place upgrade from Standard brokers to Express brokers
articles.excerpt: You can now upgrade existing Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters from Standard brokers to Express brokers in place, with fully managed data migration and no application changes. Express brokers are designed to deliver up to 3x more throughput per broker, scale up to 20x faster, and recover up to 90% faster compared to Standard brokers. With in-place upgrade, you can get the performance and operational benefits of Express brokers in hours, without needing to create a new cluster or having to migrate your data and applications to it. The upgrade keeps cluster endpoints unchanged, eliminating application cutovers, and preserves consumer offsets, so stateful applications such as Apache Flink and Kafka Streams continue without reprocessing or duplicates. Express brokers make Apache Kafka simpler to manage and more cost-effective to run at scale, with pay-as-you-go storage that scales automatically and built-in best practice defaults for higher resilience. Previously, upgrading to Express brokers meant creating a new cluster and migrating workloads to it, which required careful planning and cross-team coordination. With this launch, you can upgrade your existing Standard brokers to Express brokers in-place, without interrupting your applications, while maintaining complete control over the upgrade process. The upgrade adds Express brokers to your cluster and moves your topics to them, either automatically or in batches you control. Your Standard brokers stay in the cluster until you choose to decommission them to complete the upgrade, so you can validate your applications and roll back if needed. In-place upgrade is available for MSK Provisioned clusters running Standard brokers on Apache Kafka version 3.9 with KRaft, in all AWS Regions where Express brokers are available. You can upgrade to Express brokers on M7g or M8g instances. Express brokers on M8g deliver up to 30% cost savings compared to Express brokers on M7g. There's no additional charge for the upgrade itself. You
articles.summary: Amazon MSK permet désormais une mise à niveau in-place des brokers Standard vers Express, boostant débit et résilience sans migration ni interruption.

articles.title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region
articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region, along with Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service, that helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. Customers in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud can now run Prometheus-compatible monitoring workloads in-region, which lowers latency for local workloads and keeps metric data within the region. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector is a fully managed, agentless collector. It discovers and collects Prometheus metrics from your container workloads, so you do not need to run collection agents yourself. The collector sends metrics to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace, where you query and analyze them. A workspace is a logical space for storing and querying Prometheus metrics. For the full list of regions where Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is available, see the AWS Regional Services List . For pricing, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus pricing page . To learn more, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus user guide and the product page.
articles.summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus est désormais disponible dans le cloud souverain européen AWS (Allemagne), avec un collecteur agentless pour surveiller les métriques en local.

AWS Network Firewall introduit un mode automatisé pour sécuriser les passerelles internet des VPC, réduisant les risques de configuration manuelle.

dynamicThemes.trend: AWS Lambda publie les changements d'état des fonctions vers EventBridge, simplifiant les pipelines sans polling. Les capacités batch pour SQS FIFO passent à 10 000 messages, et Lambda MicroVMs est déployé dans 7 nouvelles régions. EventBridge Scheduler ajoute 589 actions API pour automatiser sans code.

dynamicThemes.label: Mathématiques et vérification formelle

dynamicThemes.label: Releases majeures et mises à jour critiques

Ces mises à jour incluent des corrections mineures et des améliorations de stabilité pour les pipelines de monitoring et d'observabilité.

Neptune Serverless améliore ses performances de 30% avec Graviton4 et un scaling plus précis. DynamoDB vector search ajoute des filtres avancés pour les requêtes vectorielles.
